diagnostic_evidence.quote: only a sufficient condition \eqref{eq:strongdualityRuttan} for the minimax approximant is provided in Theorem \ref{thm:strongdualityRuttan} under the assumption:  $\wtd\beta_j\ne 0~\forall j\in[\ell]$  in  the pair $(\wtd p,\wtd q)$ that achieves $d(\bw^*)$.
A remedy for this is to impose new constraints (e.g., $\sum_{j=1}^\ell|\wtd \beta_j|^2=1$, or $\wtd\beta_j\ne 0~\forall j\in[\ell]$) into \eqref{eq:linearminmax2}.

issues.failure_explanation: The barycentric form \eqref{eq:baryform} only guarantees interpolation at $t_j$ when $\beta_j\neq 0$. Equation \eqref{eq:linearminmax} minimizes over all $\alpha,\beta$ without this constraint, so its feasible set includes functions that do not satisfy the interpolation conditions. Thus it is a relaxation, not an equivalent formulation of \eqref{eq:baryInterpMinmax}.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the constraint $\beta_j\neq 0$ (or an equivalent normalization) to \eqref{eq:linearminmax}, or explicitly state it as a relaxation and restrict the dual guarantees to cases where the dual solution satisfies $\beta_j\neq 0$.
issues.overall_effect: The derived dual problem is not exactly the dual of the interpolation-constrained problem; strong duality can only be a sufficient condition under extra assumptions, and the algorithm may return non-interpolating candidates.
issues.title: Primal formulation omits nonzero barycentric weight constraint
issues.why_classification: Adding the constraint materially complicates the dual function, as the paper itself notes; the issue is more than a local typo but the paper's sufficient-condition framework remains partially valid.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the set of extreme points ${\cal X}_e(\wtd \xi)$ defined as  \eqref{eq:extremalset} contains at least $n+2-\ell$ nodes.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof asserts that linear independence of the functions $\{1/(x-t_j)\}$ allows matching $k$ arbitrary conditions. Linear independence alone does not imply the evaluation map at $k$ points is surjective. The conclusion is true but requires an additional argument that the span contains all $P(x)/\prod(x-t_j)$ with $\deg P\le n-\ell$, so polynomial interpolation can match $k\le n+1-\ell$ values.

failure_location.quote: As $\{\frac{1}{x-t_j}\}_{j=\ell+1}^{n+1}$ are $n+1-\ell$ linearly independent functions, we can choose the parameters $\{\what \alpha_j\}_{j=\ell+1}^{n+1}$ to meet the $k$ (note $k\le n+1-\ell$) conditions \eqref{eq:newp}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the standard polynomial interpolation argument showing the evaluation map is surjective for $k\le n+1-\ell$.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the lower bound $n+2-\ell$ for the number of extreme points is incomplete as written.
issues.title: Invalid inference from linear independence in extreme point proof
issues.why_classification: The theorem is true and the missing argument is standard and local; no substantive claim is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Stop and return  $\xi^*=\xi^{(k)}$ either if $k\ge k_{\rm maxit}$ or
b-d-Lawson cannot be guaranteed to handle \eqref{eq:baryInterpMinmax} in all cases.

issues.failure_explanation: The algorithm's ENSURE promises the minimax rational approximation. However, Step 4 allows stopping at the iteration cap $k_{\rm maxit}$, and the relative tolerance only checks a sufficient condition. The paper's conclusion explicitly states that b-d-Lawson cannot be guaranteed in all cases. Hence the output is at best a candidate approximation.

failure_location.quote: \ENSURE  The minimax rational approximation $\xi^*$ of \eqref{eq:baryInterpMinmax} represented in the barycentric formula \eqref{eq:optimalpq}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the ENSURE to 'candidate rational approximation', with a note that it is minimax only when the stopping criterion and strong-duality assumptions hold.
issues.overall_effect: The algorithm's stated output guarantee is false; it may return a non-minimax approximation.
issues.title: Algorithm output guarantee overclaims minimax approximation
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local change to the output contract and does not affect the algorithm's operations; the paper already provides the necessary caveat.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: for  any $ \bw\in {\cal S}$ with at least $n+1$ nonzero $w_j$'s

issues.failure_explanation: Proposition \ref{prop:dual_GEP} requires at least $n+1$ nonzero weights. The Lawson update can set weights to zero when errors vanish, and the paper's own Theorem \ref{thm:extremep-2} only guarantees $n+2-\ell$ positive weights at the optimum. For $\ell>1$, $n+2-\ell < n+1$, so the algorithm can reach a weight vector outside Proposition's hypothesis. Then the QR decomposition of $\sqrt{W}C_q$ is rank-deficient and $R_q$ is not invertible, so the prescribed computation of $d(\bw)$ fails.

failure_location.quote: Compute  $d(\bw^{(k)})$ and the associated vector $\xi^{(k)}(\bx)=\bp^{(k)}/\bq^{(k)}$   according to  Proposition \ref{prop:dual_GEP}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Modify the algorithm to handle rank-deficient weight vectors, e.g., by using a rank-revealing QR or maintaining a small positive floor on weights, or adjust Proposition's requirements.
issues.overall_effect: The computational method may break down in interpolation-constrained cases with $\ell>1$, which are a main focus of the paper.
issues.title: Algorithm may violate Proposition's nonzero weight assumption
issues.why_classification: The fix requires a contained but nontrivial change to the computational procedure to handle degenerate support, while the main idea remains.
